newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU vets Rand McNally /De Agostini deal.
newsitem.headline: EU vets Rand McNally /De Agostini deal.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it was seeking comments on a joint venture between publishing companies Rand McNally & Company of the United States and Italy's De Agostini to market, sell or license rights to maps and atlases.

It said in a notice published in the European Union's Official Journal that the deal was submitted to it for clearance in March 1996 under EU rules which ban restrictive practices or abuse of dominant position.
There is no deadline for the Commission to rule on cases falling under such rules.

The joint venture agreement, which took effect in December 1994, aims to offer to publishers worldwide atlases using the highest quality, state-of-art cartographic resources, the notice said. Canada, the United States, Italy and Switzerland are not covered by the deal.
Rand McNally is a Delaware-based company active in geographic and travel related publishing. In 1995 it also signed an worldwide contract with Reader's Digest Association Inc to market maps.
De Agostini is ultimately owned by privately-held Istituto Geographico De Agostini SpA (IGDA) which publishes magazines, books as well as maps and atlases.

Under the terms of a series of agreements submitted to the Commission, De Agostini provides accounting, property, marketing and management services to the venture. Both McNally and IGDA will provide the products to be marketed by their subsidiary. McNally also grants IGDA the exclusive right to use its technology to produce maps and atlases for the joint venture.
Interested parties have until early March to comment.
